elerian-japan-q2-gdp-carried-by-a-1_5pct:
Japan's real GDP rose 0.3 percent on the quarter, which annualizes to 1.1 percent.
That fell short of the 2.0 percent the market expected, and the components that produced it were not the ones expected either.

@@REF@@Japan Q2 growth misses forecasts on weaker spending, investment (Reuters, 2026-08-16)|https://ca.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-q2-growth-misses-forecasts-on-weaker-spending-investment-4802742|https://content-media.investing.com/trkd-images/LYNXMPEM7G00M_L.jpg

Domestic demand contributed minus 0.2 percentage points to growth.
Private consumption did not rise for the first time in eight quarters, and business investment fell 1.2 percent.

The headline still came out positive because net exports added 0.5 percentage points.
Net exports are exports minus imports, so the figure widens when imports shrink.
This quarter exports rose 0.5 percent and imports fell 1.5 percent.

Put simply, the amount households and firms stopped buying from abroad showed up as growth.

## Which line produced the plus

@@CHK@@Real GDP annualized, actual|+1.1%|Real GDP annualized, consensus|+2.0%|Prior quarter, first preliminary|+2.1%@@The 2.1 percent the original post used as its benchmark is the first preliminary reading. That number was revised twice and stood at 1.8 to 1.9 percent by the time of this release, so the actual deceleration is gentler than the comparison suggests.@@Checked 2026-08-17 · Cabinet Office ESRI first preliminary estimate for April to June 2026, released 2026-08-17; the revised prior quarter is as reported

The same day, the 10-year government bond yield climbed to 2.9 percent.
That is the highest since September 1996.
The 30-year sits near 4.1 percent and the 2-year at 1.7 percent.

Why that matters is written in the budget.
The fiscal 2026 budget totals 122.3 trillion yen, of which debt servicing takes 31.3 trillion yen, or 25.6 percent.
And the budget was drawn up assuming a 3 percent bond interest rate.

## What the intervention left, and what it erased

On August 1, Japan's Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Japan moved with the US Treasury to buy yen.
It was the first time the two countries acted together since 2011.
The yen briefly strengthened to 155.20 per dollar.

@@REF@@Japan and US confirm rare joint intervention to prop up yen (Al Jazeera, 2026-08-03)|https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/8/3/japan-and-us-confirm-rare-joint-intervention-to-prop-up-yen

Two weeks later the rate is back around 159 per dollar.
The intervention slowed the move rather than turned it, and that erosion is what the original post is pointing at.
What is left is the interest rate.

## Two readings of the same release

@@CMP@@El-Erian's reading|A miss of this size raises the weight of the domestic measures needed to support the yen, which is what makes the policy implication larger.|Japanese economists' reading|The consumption weakness owes much to one-offs such as pharmaceutical asset sales and changes to education policy and tobacco tax. The September timing does not move.

The split is over whether this quarter is structure or noise.
Kazutaka Maeda of Meiji Yasuda Research Institute does not think the data point to weakness ahead or affect the timing of the Bank of Japan's next hike.
Masato Koike of Sompo Institute Plus reads the soft consumption as a case for tightening at a more gradual pace, a disagreement about speed rather than direction.

## September 17 and 18, when the Bank of Japan sits again

The policy rate has been 1.0 percent since the hike on June 16, the highest since 1995.
The next Monetary Policy Meeting runs on September 17 and 18, and prediction markets and rate futures put the odds of a hike between 75 and 81 percent.

So what this release actually changed will be visible that day.
A hike in September means the market read the miss as noise; a pass means the minus 0.2 percentage points from domestic demand entered the Bank's arithmetic.
Either way, a budget built on a 3 percent bond rate keeps diverging from a 30-year yield above 4 percent.
kobeissi-nvidia-ports-pike-105b-lps-guar:
Nvidia has agreed to provide up to $105 billion of credit support for the land, the power and the building shell of a data center campus in Pike County, Ohio.
OpenAI will lease the campus, and only Nvidia chips will run inside it.

@@REF@@Nvidia guarantees SB Energy's PORTS-Pike technology campus in Ohio to exclusively host Nvidia AI compute (Nvidia Newsroom, 2026-08-17)|https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-guarantees-sb-energy-s-ports-pike-technology-campus-in-ohio-to-exclusively-host-nvidia-ai-compute

This is not a loan.
SB Energy, a SoftBank company, builds and owns the land, the generation and the buildings.
Nvidia's role is to stand behind that company when it borrows from lenders.

A guarantee lowers the risk the lender carries, and cheaper debt follows.
Think of a parent co-signing a child's mortgage.
The parent does not buy the house; the parent makes the bank lend at a lower rate.

## Three cuts in three weeks

@@TIME@@2026-07-27|Reports said Nvidia was weighing a backstop of up to $250 billion for a 10-gigawatt Ohio campus|2026-08-14|After investors questioned the risk exposure, reports put the figure below $120 billion|2026-08-15|Nvidia's contemplated equity investment in SB Energy was reported at $3 billion|2026-08-17|The confirmed numbers were $105 billion of credit support and $1.5 billion of equity in SB Energy|>2028|The first tranche of capacity comes online@@What shrank the number was not a regulator but Nvidia's own shareholders. The scale OpenAI wants to lease did not change; the width of the backstop did.@@Data Center Dynamics and CNBC reporting, 2026-07-27 to 2026-08-17

@@REF@@Nvidia confirms it will back 4.25GW of OpenAI capacity at Ports-Pike mega data center (Data Center Dynamics, 2026-08-17)|https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/nvidia-confirms-it-will-back-425gw-of-openai-capacity-at-ports-pike-mega-data-center/|https://media.datacenterdynamics.com/media/images/portsmouth_pike_county_ohio_dept_.2e16d0ba.fill-1200x630.png

## Between 4.25 and 8

The scope Jensen Huang wrote out himself on LinkedIn is narrow.
The support covers roughly four gigawatts over a 20-year term, and it runs to defined portions of lease and power payments plus a specified residual-value commitment.
He also wrote what it is not: not the full cost of the site, and not all of the tenant's obligations.

Eight gigawatts is the compute OpenAI intends to lease.
What has been backed today is the 4.25 gigawatts of the first phase, and the remaining 3.75 gigawatts sits as an option Nvidia may or may not take.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/BalticServers_data_center.jpg/960px-BalticServers_data_center.jpg|This is where the $105 billion points. What is guaranteed is not the chips that go into these racks but the building and the electricity that arrives here.|BalticServers.com · CC BY-SA 3.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:BalticServers_data_center.jpg

## Why land and power of all things

The campus rises on the decommissioned Portsmouth gaseous diffusion plant, a Department of Energy site in Pike County that once enriched uranium for naval reactors.

The electricity is being built from scratch.
Ten gigawatts of new generation is planned, 9.2 gigawatts of it natural gas, and SB Energy and SoftBank are putting at least $4.2 billion more into regional grid infrastructure through AEP Ohio.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Gas_stove_blue_flames.jpg/500px-Gas_stove_blue_flames.jpg|Before eight gigawatts of compute there has to be this much fire. Of the ten gigawatts of new generation, 9.2 gigawatts burns natural gas.|Marina Burity · CC BY-SA 2.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gas_stove_blue_flames.jpg

The gas plant alone is estimated at around $33 billion, and gas plant construction costs have risen 66 percent in two years.
That is the price of making a place to plug the chips in, before anyone buys a chip.

## From 2028, when Pike County switches on

Huang wrote that the guarantee becomes effective in phases.
As each data center is placed in service between 2028 and 2030 the matching slice of the guarantee comes alive, and as OpenAI makes lease payments Nvidia's remaining exposure declines.

So the weight of this promise is set in 2028, not today.
If OpenAI keeps generating the cash to pay rent, the guarantee stays paper.
If it does not, Nvidia inherits somebody else's building and somebody else's power bill.
Rather than argue about whether the structure is circular financing, watch when Nvidia puts its name on the remaining 3.75 gigawatts.
Filling that slot means it has taken the full eight gigawatts onto its own risk; leaving it empty means 4.25 gigawatts is the limit Nvidia chose.

President Trump wrote on social media early on August 17 that he had instructed his war secretary to substantially reduce joint military exercises with South Korea.
That same morning, the exercise began on schedule.

@@REF@@Trump orders Pentagon to 'substantially' reduce S. Korea-US military exercises (Korea Herald, 2026-08-17)|https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10842934|https://wimg.heraldcorp.com/news/cms/2026/08/17/news-p.v1.20260817.769c976630714b66961cd7c625a73ecc_T1.jpg

The drill is Ulchi Freedom Shield, running eleven days from August 17 to 27 with about 18,000 South Korean troops taking part.
Seoul's defense ministry said the exercise is proceeding on its originally planned schedule and scale, and that it had received no request from Washington to cut it back.

## Two earlier attempts

@@TIME@@2018-06-18|The Pentagon suspends all planning for that August's Ulchi Freedom Guardian|2019-03-04|Key Resolve and Foal Eagle are replaced by a smaller exercise named Dong Maeng|2026-08-17|Ulchi Freedom Shield begins; the same day Trump orders a substantial reduction|>2026-11|Target date for completing full operational capability verification at the alliance meeting@@Neither earlier episode made the exercises disappear; both changed their size and their name. If this one sits in the same place, the result is a smaller next edition rather than a cancellation.@@Retrieved 2026-08-17 · Defense News and AP, 2018-06-18 · The Diplomat, 2019-03-03 · Kyunghyang Shinmun, 2026-08-07

This form of announcement is not new.
After the 2018 Singapore summit the Pentagon suspended all planning for that August's drill, and in 2019 Key Resolve and Foal Eagle were swapped out for a slimmed-down exercise called Dong Maeng.
Neither ended the exercises; both changed their scale and their label.

## The saving was $14 million

Trump wrote that the United States pays much of the cost of these exercises.
When the 2018 drill was called off, the Pentagon put the American saving at $14 million.
Against a defense budget then running near $700 billion, the share ends below the decimal point.

The real cost-sharing sits somewhere else.
South Korea's contribution to stationing US forces is 1.5192 trillion won for 2026, 8.3% above the 1.4028 trillion won paid in 2025.
From 2027 through 2030 it is indexed to consumer inflation with the annual rise capped at 5%.

@@REF@@Trump orders Pentagon to scale back joint exercises with South Korea (AP via NPR, 2026-08-17)|https://www.npr.org/2026/08/17/g-s1-138969/trump-exercises-south-korea|https://npr.brightspotcdn.com/dims3/default/strip/false/crop/7269x4089+0+385/resize/1400/quality/85/format/jpeg/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fnpr-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F67%2F19%2F6160c4e9465faf5b3cc8cf1de9d5%2Fap26228725686076.jpg

The same report noted that Hegseth himself praised South Korea's higher defense spending in May as a model of alliance burden-sharing.
Three months separate that praise from an order that complains about cost.

## Why the drill is tied to a verification

@@FLOW@@Smaller joint exercise|Fewer chances for South Korea to lead|Full operational capability check|That capability is only tested inside a joint exercise|Command transfer target year|Set at the November alliance meeting@@The exercise is not a ceremony; it is an input to a verification procedure. Shrink it and there is less evidence to verify with, which makes an earlier target year harder to defend.@@Retrieved 2026-08-17

Wartime operational control is the authority to command South Korean forces in a war, and it currently rests with the commander of the combined forces.
One condition for handing that authority to South Korea is a full operational capability verification confirming that its military can run combined operations.

That verification happens only inside a joint exercise.
Yet the two sides had already agreed that this year's Ulchi Freedom Shield would run without South Korea in the lead, with verification targeted for completion by the November alliance meeting.
An order to shrink the exercise lands on top of that schedule.

## The August 18 open is the first answer

Korean markets were shut on August 17 for a substitute Liberation Day holiday, so there is no price yet for this announcement.
On August 14, the last session before it, the KOSPI had risen for five straight days and was approaching 7,000.

The test is not the name of the drill but November.
If the alliance meeting delivers both a completed capability verification and a target year for the command transfer, this order was a negotiating line.
If the verification slips to a later date, the reduction reached the procedure itself, and cost-sharing talks and troop numbers come onto the same page.
That is also where Korean defense shares split on this news. A thinner alliance reads as a bigger domestic procurement budget, but an actual troop cut puts regional risk back into the price.

@@BAR@@One bitcoin, August 2021|25.0 ounces of gold|25.02|One bitcoin, August 2026|14.5 ounces of gold|14.50@@This is the weight of gold one bitcoin buys. One bitcoin bought 25.0 ounces in 2021, rose to 35.2 ounces by August last year, and buys 14.5 ounces now.

Inside one sentence the direction is right and the period is wrong.

Silver draws on industrial and investment demand at once, so it moves further than gold on the same news.

@@CMP@@Schiff's reading|Money that left paper currency is now leaving digital paper too, and going into gold and silver.|Kitco's stated reason|July retail sales fell 0.6%, cutting September hike odds from 34% to 29%.

@@REF@@Bitcoin ETFs record largest outflow in six weeks as token stagnates (Bloomberg, 2026-08-17)|https://www.business-standard.com/markets/cryptocurrency/bitcoin-etfs-record-largest-outflow-in-six-weeks-as-token-stagnates-126081700466_1.html|https://bsmedia.business-standard.com/_media/bs/img/article/2026-08/17/thumb/fitandfill/1200X628/1786950115-6145.jpg

hanke-fao-food-index-3yr-high-veg-oil-vs:
The UN Food and Agriculture Organization's July food price index, published August 7, came in at 131.1, the highest reading since January 2023.
Its vegetable oil index rose to 195.7, up 17.3% from a year earlier and the highest since June 2022.

@@REF@@World food prices hit 3-year high in July as weather and war weigh, FAO says (Reuters, 2026-08-07)|https://whbl.com/2026/08/07/world-food-prices-hit-3-year-high-in-july-as-weather-and-war-weigh-fao-says/|https://storage.googleapis.com/media.mwcradio.com/mimesis/2026-08/07/2026-08-07T080417Z_1_LYNXMPEM760K5_RTROPTP_3_GLOBAL-INFLATION-FAO.JPG

Steve Hanke took those two numbers the same day and called them collateral damage from the US-Israeli war on Iran.
The numbers match the FAO release. What FAO itself wrote down as the causes runs wider than that one line.

## Oil rose, milk fell

The food price index bundles international trade prices for five groups: cereals, vegetable oils, meat, dairy and sugar.
In July those five did not move together.

Cereals rose 3.4% on the month and stand 6.9% above a year ago, and sugar rose 5.6% on the month.
Meat went the other way, down 2.8%, and dairy fell 24.8% from a year earlier.

So the headline index is only 1.0% higher than a year ago.
Inside the same table, milk is giving back what cooking oil is adding.

## What Indonesia changed on July 1

@@TIME@@2026-01|Indonesia decides to hold the blending mandate at 40%, citing the cost to the budget|2026-03-30|Reverses toward 50% as the gap between palm oil and diesel narrows|2026-07-01|The 50% biodiesel mandate takes effect; the palm export levy also rises from 10% to 12.5%|2026-08-07|FAO's July food price index prints 131.1, the highest since January 2023|>2026-09-04|Next FAO food price index release@@The index reached a three-year high in the very month the mandate went up. With the dates in that order, policy and war have to be weighed separately.@@Retrieved 2026-08-17 · FAO Food Price Index, 2026-08-07 · Argus Media, 2026-03-30 · Fuels & Lubes Asia

Biodiesel is a fuel made by treating a vegetable oil such as palm so it can stand in for diesel.
Indonesia sets by law how much of it must be blended into diesel, and that share went from 40% to 50% on July 1.

When the share goes up, dinner tables and fuel tanks compete for the same palm oil.
Higher crude prices sharpen that competition, because when diesel is expensive, blending pays even without a subsidy.

@@REF@@Indonesia targets 50pc biodiesel blend in 2026 (Argus Media, 2026-03-30)|https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2807730-indonesia-targets-50pc-biodiesel-blend-in-2026

Jakarta settled on holding at 40% in January and then reversed the decision in March.
The reasons it gave were the narrowing spread between palm oil and diesel, and supply disruption in the Middle East.
The war enters here as the force that pushed a policy along.

## Why did sunflower oil fall

Read FAO's own wording and palm oil rose for a second month on firm Indonesian biodiesel demand and higher crude prices, while soy oil rose on steady feedstock demand from fuel.
Sunflower and rapeseed oil, by contrast, fell in July. FAO notes only that renewed Black Sea tension limited the decline.

If war were the force lifting cooking oil, the oil closest to a front line should have risen first.
Instead that one fell, and the ones that rose were the tropical oils with a policy bid under them.

@@CMP@@Hanke's reading|A three-year high and a 17% jump in cooking oil are collateral damage from the war on Iran.|FAO's table's reading|Palm oil rose on Indonesia's mandate and crude; sunflower oil, nearest the Black Sea, fell.

Looking at the same index, one side sees a front line and the other sees a decree issued in Jakarta.

## What $89 Brent leaves behind

The two forces can be sized against each other.
Brent traded near $89 a barrel on August 17, 33.9% above a year ago, while the vegetable oil index is up 17.3% over the same span.
If crude is the channel through which the war reaches food, only about half of crude's gain has come through.

What is left to settle sits with Indonesia.
If the September 4 release shows the oil component climbing again while Brent stays flat, the mandate set the price, not the war.
If crude slides and cooking oil holds, the bid under it is demand fixed by law.
Either way, the input costs of palm traders and of the food companies that fry with the stuff are tied to Jakarta's decision for longer than to the headlines from the war.

The price of indium phosphide substrate is going up for a fourth time.
The average six-inch wafer has already climbed to around $5,000, a rise of 250 percent, and the fourth-quarter increase is reported to be more than 10 percent.

@@REF@@China's control over indium phosphide exports threatens AI data centre rollout (Mining.com, 2026-06-11)|https://www.mining.com/web/chinas-control-over-indium-phosphide-exports-threatens-ai-data-centre-rollout/|https://www.mining.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/AdobeStock_1598677550-scaled-e1781193655577.jpeg

Suppliers have said buyers may not get the material even if they have the money.
That is a sentence you rarely hear about a semiconductor input.

@@BAR@@Two-inch substrate, early 2025|about $800|800|Two-inch substrate, April 2026|about $2,400|2400@@The price tripled and the number of companies able to make it did not change.@@BigGo Finance (2026-04-25) · checked 2026-08-17

## The colors an optical fiber likes

At each end of the cable running between data center racks sits a part about the size of a finger.
Inside that part, called an optical transceiver, an electrical signal becomes light.
The laser that actually produces that light is grown on a base of indium phosphide.

Optical fiber does not carry every color of light equally well.
At 1310 nanometers the signal does not spread, and at 1550 nanometers the least of it leaks away.
Long-distance optical links therefore use only these two wavelengths.

This is why silicon cannot take over the job.
Silicon converts electricity into light so inefficiently that it never becomes a laser, and gallium arsenide does emit light but in the 850 to 980 nanometer range, which is not a color the fiber likes.
Put simply, indium phosphide is close to the only material that can produce the colors the fiber will carry.

It is also why the spread of silicon photonics increases demand for indium phosphide rather than reducing it.
The path the light travels can be etched in silicon, but the place where the light is made still needs a separate indium phosphide chip attached.

@@REF@@Lumentum CEO warns of impending bottleneck on critical material used for silicon photonics (Tom's Hardware, 2026-07-31)|https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/semiconductors/lumentum-ceo-says-the-indium-phosphide-shortage-will-become-worse-than-memory|https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ibEpXbFzhNegj42rkqPzgZ-1920-80.jpg

Michael Hurlston, chief executive of the optical component maker Lumentum, said supply currently falls more than 30 percent short of customer demand.
He said the shortage would become worse than the one in memory.
Lumentum's revenue in the same quarter was $808.4 million, up 90 percent from a year earlier.

## Only three places make it

@@SHARE@@Sumitomo Electric|43%|43|AXT|35%|35|JX Advanced Metals|13%|13|Everyone else|9%|9@@Three companies hold 91 percent. That is why a higher price does not immediately bring more material.@@BigGo Finance (2026-04-25) tally · checked 2026-08-17

A different set of companies takes the substrate and grows a thin crystal layer on top of it.
The process is called epitaxy and the product an epitaxial wafer.
The Taiwanese firms the post named as beneficiaries, Visual Photonics Epitaxy and Landmark Optoelectronics, sit at this step.

When substrate prices rise, the price of these wafers follows.
They have already risen twice, and a third increase is reported to be under discussion for the fourth quarter.

## There is a second hand on the price

The post reads the increase as demand outrunning supply.
But this material has a second hand on its price that moves regardless of demand.

AXT, second by share, runs its plant in Beijing.
Its subsidiary Beijing Tongmei needs an export license from China's commerce ministry for each shipment of indium phosphide substrate.
Licenses came slowly in the fourth quarter of 2025 and revenue was held down; they widened during 2026 and revenue jumped.
First-quarter revenue was $26.9 million, of which indium phosphide was $13.6 million.
Second-quarter revenue rose to $47.6 million with net income of $11.1 million.

The raw material points the same way.
About 70 percent of refined indium output sits in China, and the spot price reached $500 to $600 per kilogram in February 2026, the highest since 2015.

## Where AXT's third quarter decides it

So does this price increase reach the seller's income statement, or does it stop at a quoted price with material that cannot ship?
The same quarterly report separates the two.

If AXT's third-quarter revenue exceeds the second quarter, the increase actually reached the invoice.
If it does not, the price rose while export licenses or capacity held the volume back.
With this material, raising the price and collecting it are not the same event.
serenity-mlcc-crowding-out-taiyo-yuden-1:
Lines were retooled to make more of the high-grade capacitors that AI servers need, and the ordinary capacitors that go into phones and laptops started running short.
Serenity expects that squeeze to bite in earnest late in the second half of 2026 or early in 2027.

## Capacitors come in grades

An MLCC is a fingernail-sized part built from stacked ceramic layers.
It holds a little charge and releases it, smoothing the power that runs through a circuit.

MLCCs are graded by how little their capacitance drifts as temperature swings.
X5R drifts more but is cheap and made in volume, which is why it fills phones and laptops.
X6S and X7R hold steadier across a wider temperature range, are harder to build, and go onto AI server boards.

That is the crux.

The two grades mostly come off the same lines rather than separate plants.
Every hour spent printing the upper grade is an hour not spent on the lower one.

## What dries up in the space left behind

Serenity reported that channel checks in China's electronics market found 22 microfarad and 47 microfarad parts out of stock,
and that some manufacturers had stopped taking orders altogether.
The post also noted Walsin of Taiwan citing 22 microfarad among the high-volume specifications used in smartphones and PCs.

@@REF@@Across-the-board 30% price hike: MLCC price surge intensifies (TrendForce, 2026-08-04)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/08/04/news-across-the-board-30-price-hike-mlcc-price-surge-intensifies/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/24142311/Samsung-Electro-Mechanics-MLCC-20260224-624x416.jpg

That report confirms the same movement from a different angle.
Channel inventory for general-purpose parts from 1 to 22 microfarad has fallen below the 30-day warning line,
and consumer-grade X5R capacity is being converted to the high-end specifications AI demands.
The shortage, in other words, has not stayed inside the AI grade.

The "15% or below" in Hanke's post is a number that moves with the ruler you pick.

Measured as gross value added, the series India's own statistics office publishes, manufacturing has drifted between 16% and 18%.
Measured as a share of gross domestic product, the basis the World Bank uses so countries can be compared, it falls to around 12%.

This is where the reading usually goes wrong.

A flat share does not mean manufacturing failed to grow.
Manufacturing output itself has expanded at roughly 6% a year since 2021.
Services simply expanded at close to 8% over the same stretch.

A share is a fraction.
When the numerator grows and the denominator grows faster, the ratio falls.

Not everything can be blamed on the denominator, though.
Of 23 manufacturing sub-sectors, 11 produced less in 2024-25 than they did in 2018-19.
The aggregate rose because a handful of sectors carried the rest.

## The iPhones really were built in India

A stalled share does not mean the policy changed nothing.

The Production Linked Incentive scheme, launched in 2021, committed 1.97 trillion rupees, about $22.8 billion, across 14 sectors.
Investment actually realised through March 2025 was counted at 1.76 trillion rupees.

According to that report, Apple's vendors assembled $22 billion worth of iPhones in India in fiscal 2025,

Foxconn and Tata Electronics divide the volume between them.

The gap is in the size of the board.
Incentives actually disbursed over the same period came to 215 billion rupees, about 11% of the money set aside.
The promise was large and the execution was small.

The dispute matters because it splits how an investor can own Indian manufacturing.
One way assumes the target eventually gets filled and buys Indian industry broadly.
The other ignores the share entirely and buys only the narrow boxes where volume genuinely rose, electronics and semiconductors.
The record of the last twelve years favours the second.

China is buying roughly twice as much Korean dried laver as it did two years ago.
Figures released by Korea's Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries on August 16 show shipments to China rising from 2,543 tons in 2024 to 4,539 tons in 2025,

The odd part is that China grows more laver than any other country on earth.

## Chinese laver cannot become a seasoned sheet

Laver comes in species, and the species decides what it can become.
Most of what China farms is the warm-water variety Pyropia haitanensis.
It grows where the sea is too warm for anything else, but the sheet it makes is thick and chewy,
so it ends up in soup rather than in the thin roasted sheets sold as a snack.

Korea and Japan farm Pyropia yezoensis, which is the opposite.
It grows only in cold water and comes out thin enough that oil, salt and a pass over heat give you the brittle sheet most people picture when they think of seasoned laver.

That is the first reason China buys Korean dried laver.

Meru offers a different reason.
Chinese coastal water, he writes, is polluted badly enough to keep the product out of export markets.
China's own published numbers point the other way.

@@CHK@@Coastal water rated good, 2024|83.7%|Coastal water rated poor, 2024|8.6%|Rated good, 2023|85.0%@@A number close to 84% does turn up. There is a real research literature on heavy metals, cadmium in particular, off the Jiangsu coast.
What the official bulletin does not support is the wider claim that the coastline as a whole cannot grow export-grade laver.

## The money sits in the seasoning step

@@BAR@@Dried laver, bundle of 100 sheets|8,500 won|8500|Seasoned laver, same bundle|25,000 won|25000@@It is the same seaweed. One step, brushing it with oil and salt and toasting it, nearly triples the price. China buys at the first number and sells at the second.@@Retrieved 2026-08-17 · Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries data of 2026-08-16, as reported by the Korea Economic Daily

Chinese processors import Korean dried sheets, brush them with oil and salt in the Korean style,
print a Korean-language brand on the package and ship them out again.
The raw material is Korean, so the taste barely differs, and the price is lower.

Seasoned laver has fallen from 43.2% of Korea's laver export volume in 2020 to 35.3% in 2025.
Over those same five years the volume of dried laver Korea exports rose 82%.
Korea is selling more and keeping less of what each sheet is worth.

## Washington waived the tariff on the seasoned kind

@@REF@@Seasoned gim exempt from US tariff (The Korea Times, 2025-12-14)|https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/companies/20251214/seasoned-gim-exempt-from-us-tariff|https://newsimg.koreatimes.co.kr/2025/12/14/97ad6446-f4be-4867-aad8-a4be4973bfa5.jpg

On November 13, 2025 the United States dropped the 15% tariff it charged on seasoned laver.
Dried laver still carries the 15%.

Korea sold $228 million of laver into the United States through November last year, roughly 90% of it seasoned,

Total laver exports through the same month came to $1.04 billion, the first time the figure has passed a billion dollars in a year.

The step where the price triples and the step where the tariff disappeared are the same step.
If Chinese processors fill it, what is left for Korea is supplying the input.

In June the ministry published a supply-chain plan for laver exports built around a “Made in Korea” national certification mark.
The point of the mark is to separate Korean seasoned laver from Chinese product wearing a Korean-language label,

If the mark creates a real distinction on American shelves, the seasoned share climbs back.
If the 2026 annual figures instead put it below 35.3%,
Korea has slid one more step from selling the finished good toward selling the input.

In the year laver exports first passed a billion dollars, the question worth asking is not how much Korea sold.
It is which step Korea sold.

The reason the two numbers diverge this far is simple.
Korea's consumer price index has no line for house prices at all.

What an index does not count did not happen as far as the index is concerned.

## How a price index counts a home

The only housing components in the Korean index are jeonse and monthly rent.
Jeonse carries a weight of 5.4% and monthly rent 4.5%, and together they do not reach 10%.

The United States counts it differently.
Homeowners are asked what their house would fetch if they rented it out, and that figure goes into the index.
This is called owners' equivalent rent: in plain terms, the rent you are treated as paying yourself to live in your own home.

@@BAR@@Housing rent in Korea's consumer price index|9.9%|9.91|Shelter in the US consumer price index|35.6%|35.6@@Two indexes with the same name give housing this much difference in space. When house prices rise, the American index records at least part of it through rental value.
The Korean index has no box for it, so it records nothing.

## And what it does record, it records late

Jeonse and monthly rent contracts usually run two years.
Statistics Korea surveys not only newly signed contracts but the entire stock of existing ones.

So even when market rents rise, the index does not move until renewals come around.
Today's rent increases show up in inflation one to two years from now.

## The tap opened on August 13

@@REF@@Korea doubles the household loan growth target to 3% (Seoul Economic Daily, 2026-08-13)|https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/08/13/korea-doubles-2025-household-loan-growth-target-to-3|https://wimg.sedaily.com/news/cms/2026/08/13/news-p.v1.20260806.cf902aeb0974402e9d7df7646d865e63_P1.jpg

Behind the measure was congestion at the lending window.
The five major banks blew through their annual quotas in July, leaving roughly 70,000 households due to move into new apartments in the second half struggling to get balance-payment loans, and queues formed outside branches before dawn.

The package also contains a clause pulling the other way.
Guarantee ratios on jeonse loans for owners who live away from the home they own were cut from 80% to 70% in Seoul to push them into occupying it, which shrinks the pool of homes offered for lease.
That is the clause the Hyundai Research Institute singled out when it put second-half inflation at 2.7% and said it could reach 3% if the risks materialize.

## What the Bank of Korea faces on August 27

The Bank of Korea held rates eight meetings in a row and then raised the base rate by 25 basis points on July 16.
It was the first hike in three years, and the dot plot published afterwards had 10 of the 21 board members at 3.0% by year-end.

The financial regulator is releasing credit so genuine buyers can close on their apartments, while the central bank has to restrain the debt and the house prices that credit creates.
Two arms of the same state are now pulling in opposite directions.
Household debt is already estimated to have passed 2,000 trillion won for the first time.
The absence of house prices from the index works against the Bank of Korea in this standoff.
Quiet measured inflation weakens the case for raising rates, while asset prices and debt keep growing outside what that quiet measure covers.

So the place to watch is the rent index from August onward.
If the base rate reaches 3.0% or higher by year-end, the side effects of the August 13 package moved monetary policy; if it stays where the July hike left it, the gap between the two institutions never showed up in the rate.

@@REF@@Long bond rout drives TLT ETF to lows unseen since 2004 (Benzinga, 2026-08-14)|https://www.benzinga.com/markets/bonds/26/08/61223284/bond-market-rout-tlt-etf-lowest-level-since-2004

The policy rate and the 30-year bond share a name and little else.
What the Fed sets is the price of money banks lend each other overnight. The 30-year is the price of money lent today against a promise to repay in three decades.
The Fed sets the first. Buyers and sellers set the second.

## So what actually moved

@@CHK@@30-year Treasury|5.21%|10-year Treasury|4.63%|2-year Treasury|4.15%|10-year breakeven inflation|2.27%|30-year real yield|2.97%|Fed funds upper bound|3.75%@@The upper bound of the policy rate is 3.75 percent and the 30-year sits at 5.21 percent. Breakeven inflation stays on the low side, so what pushed the long bond up is the real yield rather than the inflation outlook. That points somewhere other than the cause Bilello names.@@Checked 2026-08-17 · FRED (DGS30, DGS10, DGS2, T10YIE, DFII30; observations 2026-08-13 to 08-14) · Fed funds upper bound from FRED DFEDTARU

The real yield is the nominal yield minus expected inflation.
When it rises, borrowing money for a long time has become expensive on its own terms, whatever prices are doing.

Bilello reads the rise as inflation refusing to let the Fed go.
Yet the ten-year breakeven the market is pricing sits in the middle of the 2 percent range.
If the inflation outlook is quiet and only the long bond is climbing, what went up is not the price of inflation but the price of tying money up for a long time.

That price is called the term premium.
The New York Fed's estimate of the ten-year term premium was reported at 0.8 percent in May 2026.
During the zero rate years the same estimate was negative.

## We could not verify the 63 percent

The longest duration bond ETF Bilello refers to appears to be a fund holding very long Treasuries that pay no coupon along the way.
We could not verify the claim of a 63 percent decline from the March 2020 peak against source data.

What we could verify is the fund next to it.
TLT, which holds Treasuries of 20 years and longer, is down about 52 percent from its 2020 peak at $81.80, its lowest since 2004.

The record low yield is also slightly off.
Bilello wrote 0.8 percent for March 2020.
On FRED's daily close the lowest day is March 9, 2020, and the value that day fell just short of 1 percent.

@@TIME@@2020-03-09|The 30-year yield hit 0.99 percent, a record low on a daily close basis|2024-09-18|The Fed began cutting. The 30-year was below 4 percent|2025-12-10|A sixth cut took the policy rate's upper bound to 3.75 percent, and there have been no cuts since|2026-08-13|A $25 billion 30-year auction cleared at 5.216 percent, the highest since 2001@@The policy rate came down while the 30-year rose more than four percentage points across these four dates.@@FRED (DGS30, DFEDTARU) · US Treasury 30-year auction result, 2026-08-13 · checked 2026-08-17

The reason the drawdown is this large is duration.
Duration measures how far a bond's price moves when yields move one percentage point, and it grows with maturity.
A bond that pays no interest along the way has all of its repayment stacked at the very end, which gives it the longest duration of all.
Put simply, the same rise in yields cuts deeper the longer the maturity.

Counting reinvested interest narrows the loss.
TLT's five-year total return is reported at minus 27.4 percent.

## What the August 13 auction left behind

So is a 30-year above 5 percent a signal that inflation is unbeaten, or that tying money up for a long time has become expensive?
The August 13 auction shows half of the answer.

@@REF@@Treasury pays 5.216% on 30-year bond, costliest long debt since 2001 (PrimeRates, 2026-08-14)|https://primerates.com/treasury-pays-5-216-percent-30-year-bond-costliest-since-2001/|https://primerates.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/news-2026-08-14-hero.jpg

The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.39, below the recent average of 2.43 to 2.44, and dealers were left with 11.5 percent against an average of 10.6 percent.
Dealers taking more means fewer other buyers showed up.
Indirect bidders, the usual proxy for foreign demand, took 66.8 percent against an average of 67.0 percent.
What went missing was domestic, not foreign.

If breakeven inflation stays where it is from here and the 30-year still rises, what lifted it is the term premium and not prices.
If breakevens rise alongside it, Bilello's reading is the right one.
Whether the Fed's cuts ever reach mortgage rates and corporate long-term funding costs lies on the far side of that fork.

The phrase "circular financing" was attached to the announcement almost immediately.

## Where does the money come from

@@FLOW@@Outside investors|Third-party capital such as pension funds and insurers flows into the six managers' platforms|Platforms|That money buys GPUs and parks them inside special purpose vehicles|AI companies|Frontier AI labs and AI cloud operators rent those GPUs|Usage fees|The fees coming in repay the bonds issued against the GPUs@@Nvidia puts up money at none of these four stops. Hyperscalers are the large operators that build data centers themselves and sell the capacity as cloud.
Until now they paid for GPUs in cash, all at once, and this year that has become harder.
Alphabet has guided to $180-190 billion of capital spending for the year and Meta to $125-145 billion.
Put simply, the price of what they want to buy has started to exceed the cash they generate in a year.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/NVIDIA_GPU.jpg/960px-NVIDIA_GPU.jpg|This is the thing being pledged. The six platforms buy this board, place it in a special purpose vehicle, and issue bonds against it.|Mickael Courtiade · CC BY 2.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NVIDIA_GPU.jpg

## The auto loan analogy

@@CMP@@Michael Burry's reading|Like the $87.9 billion of purchase commitments hyperscalers have made to each other, the money is circling rather than multiplying|Jukan's reading|A carmaker that offers auto loans is not buying its own cars. It has given a customer short of cash another way to pay

The two readings part over where the money comes from.

@@REF@@Michael Burry sounds the alarm again: AI is a circular financing web with Nvidia in the middle (24/7 Wall St., 2026-08-13)|https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/13/michael-burry-sounds-the-alarm-again-ai-is-a-circular-financing-web-with-nvidia-in-the-middle/|https://247wallst.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/GettyImages-498541178-scaled.jpg

What Burry points at is the set of commitments hyperscalers made to buy from each other.
What Jukan points at is pension and insurance money arriving from outside that circle.
One is counting where the revenue came from, the other where the funding came from.

## The number 25 percent

What Nvidia actually contributed to this structure is not cash but a promise.
If the residual value of the pledged GPUs falls, Nvidia covers up to 25 percent of the decline.

Residual value is what a used asset is still worth when you sell it later.
When that value collapses, the collateral stops working as collateral and the bondholder takes the loss.
Nvidia has agreed to absorb part of that decline itself.
Jensen Huang is reported to have said the ratio is far lower than in other compute financing agreements.

A carmaker attaching a loan does not go this far.

Lending against GPUs has already started.

It was the first GPU-backed financing to carry an investment grade rating.

So is this money that widens the market, or money that props up revenue?
The answer is held by how far used GPU prices fall.

Fitch is reported to be still consulting publicly on how GPU depreciation should feed into bond ratings.
An unsettled rating standard means the cost of raising this money is also unsettled.

If used GPU prices stay inside the guaranteed band, Nvidia's guarantee stays a name on paper.
Past that line it lands on Nvidia's income statement as a real cost.
That is where the structure that let others buy Nvidia's product with someone else's money gets its price.
semianalysis-pjm-reserve-model-3_8gw-vs-:
The largest electricity market in the United States will hold an auction from September 30 to buy more power plants.
An analysis now argues that this market is undercounting the generating capacity it already has by 3.8 gigawatts.

@@REF@@PJM files backstop auction plan at FERC to meet capacity shortfall (Utility Dive, 2026-08-03)|https://www.utilitydive.com/news/pjm-backstop-capacity-auction-ferc-data-centers/826792/|https://imgproxy.divecdn.com/9mc3NVqI62Ic8RIYSCYVrATgz4o1J-WyWFfhCuMzTfM/g:ce/rs:fit:770:435/Z3M6Ly9kaXZlc2l0ZS1zdG9yYWdlL2RpdmVpbWFnZS9HZXR0eUltYWdlcy0yMTYxODUwNjkxXzEuanBn.webp

PJM runs the grid that serves 13 states and Washington, DC, home to 66 million people.
Electricity bills there have risen between 10% and 25% over the past year depending on the state.

SemiAnalysis argues that a large share of that increase is the product of an arithmetic error.

## There is a separate market for buying power plants

What changes hands in this auction is not electricity but readiness.
Generators are paid in advance to stand available for the moment they are needed, and that arrangement is called a capacity market.

Think of it as paying for a fire station.
The trucks and crews cost money every year whether or not a fire breaks out.

So the price in this market is set not by the electricity actually consumed but by how large a shortfall the operator calculates.

## Power plants get stronger in winter

A gas plant produces more electricity in cold air.
Cold air is denser, so the same turbine can push out up to 25% more power.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Gas_stove_blue_flames.jpg/500px-Gas_stove_blue_flames.jpg|The asset at the center of this card. The same plant generates more electricity in midwinter than it does in summer.|Marina Burity · CC BY-SA 2.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gas_stove_blue_flames.jpg

There is a second piece.
After Winter Storm Elliott knocked out 13% of Eastern Interconnection capacity at once in December 2022, roughly 400 of PJM's approximately 700 gas plants spent money on winterization.

SemiAnalysis argues that PJM's model still reflects neither of these.
Counting them, the firm estimates, would put 3.8 gigawatts more on the system, the equivalent of eight large gas plants.

## Who the bill for the increase was addressed to

@@CHK@@Total cost of the last four capacity auctions|$63.6 billion|Share the market monitor attributes to data centers|$29.4 billion|Clearing price, 2028/29 auction|$333.44 per MW-day@@Data centers have already been named as the culprit behind rising bills, and their share is close to half. The modeling problem SemiAnalysis points to is a candidate for explaining the other half.@@Monitoring Analytics, PJM's independent market monitor, as reported by Utility Dive 2026-07-20 · PJM 2028/29 Base Residual Auction results · retrieved 2026-08-17

@@REF@@Data centers drove $6.3B in PJM capacity auction costs, market monitor says (Utility Dive, 2026-07-20)|https://www.utilitydive.com/news/pjm-data-centers-capacity-auction-imm-bowring/825626/|https://imgproxy.divecdn.com/oSOhdb7tT_-vuiArR7FEl0Exy4T6Odfupucyli8Mb9Q/g:ce/rs:fit:770:435/Z3M6Ly9kaXZlc2l0ZS1zdG9yYWdlL2RpdmVpbWFnZS9TY3JlZW5zaG90XzE5OC5wbmc=.webp

The market monitor calculated that 38% of the cost of the 2028/29 auction was driven by data centers.
PJM itself forecasts that 30 of the 32 gigawatts of peak demand growth through 2030 will come from data centers.

The two explanations do not exclude each other.
Demand really is growing quickly, and undercounting supply on top of that makes the gap look bigger than it is.

## The auction on September 30 supplies the answer

@@TIME@@December 2022|Winter Storm Elliott takes out 13% of Eastern Interconnection capacity|December 30, 2024|Pennsylvania's governor files a complaint at FERC over the auction design|July 31, 2026|PJM files its emergency auction plan at FERC|>September 30, 2026|The emergency auction opens@@The argument over these bills is now in its fourth year on the same grid. So far it has been conducted in assertions; this auction answers in prices.@@Utility Dive and American Public Power Association reporting · retrieved 2026-08-17

PJM intends to procure 6.8 gigawatts in this emergency auction.
The 3.8 gigawatts SemiAnalysis believes are already there would cover more than half of that.

The auction signs 15-year contracts, and the price cap has been raised to $555 per MW-day.
Its weak link is that no large customer has yet committed to pay for the power.
If the contracts are signed and no buyer for that electricity appears, the cost lands back on residential bills.

So the clearing price due on December 2 is the first scorecard in this argument.
If it runs all the way to the $555 cap, the shortfall is real rather than a modeling artifact; if it settles below the cap, there was slack on the system that nobody had counted.

Who buys it, and at what price, is written into the contracts.

@@REF@@SanDisk lays out long-term supply agreements with eight customers and FY2028-2030 targets at its investor day (SanDisk Newsroom, 2026-08-13)|https://www.sandisk.com/company/newsroom/press-releases/2026/2026-08-13-sandisk-investor-day-2026|https://www.sandisk.com/content/dam/sandisk/en-us/assets/company/newsroom/press-release/2026/inv-day26.png

## Where NAND actually ends up

The same instrument is spreading into DRAM.

@@REF@@China's CXMT wins $3 billion memory supply deal with Tencent (Reuters, 2026-06-29)|https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/exclusivechinas-cxmt-wins-3-billion-memory-supply-deal-with-tencent-sources-say-4764321|https://content-media.investing.com/news/moved_LYNXMPEHAA07B_L.jpg

The original post dates that deal to last month; the signing Reuters reported exclusively was on June 29.
The month matters because it means the spread of these contracts did not follow SanDisk's presentation. It was already under way before it.

## Why Wedbush left its target where it was

Several brokers raised their price targets after the investor day. Wedbush did not.

@@REF@@Wedbush isn't fully buying SanDisk's story (Yahoo Finance / TheStreet, 2026-08-15)|https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/wedbush-isnt-fully-buying-sandisks-011700680.html|https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/B7BDAED1D6E9616FCEC98FE12A5DB803FADBAEA3BCEDF98E05456824EF5FBBAB/subgraphmysterio/resizefill_w1200_h800;quality_80;format_webp/https:%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fthestreet_881%2Fd7cfab6853826e09dad1239756eb25c1.jpg

Its reason is the age of the contracts themselves.
None of today's long-term agreements has yet lived through a stretch of falling memory prices.
Whether a buyer honors the paper when the spot price halves, or comes back asking to rewrite the terms, has not been tested.
Announced capacity additions and Chinese competition sit in the same untested column.
The argument is not that the margins are wrong, but that the machinery meant to protect them has not sat an exam.

macro-week-2026-08-16:
The US Index of Financial Conditions has climbed to 1.29 points, the easiest reading since 1997.
Borrowing and deploying money has not been this cheap in three decades.
Yet the labour and household numbers released the same week pointed the other way.

@@REF@@US Index of Financial Conditions at 1.29 points, easiest since 1997 (The Kobeissi Letter, 2026-08-14)|https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2088255853052780874

## What "easy" actually means

A financial conditions index bundles interest rates, corporate bond spreads, share prices and the dollar into a single number that answers one question: how hard is it to get money right now.

Think of it as the height of a doorstep across the whole market.
When the step is low, borrowing is easy, and buying something with that borrowed money is easy too.

Two things pushed the index up.
Equities hit all-time highs, and corporate bond spreads stayed near their tightest since 1998.
A spread is the extra yield a weaker borrower must pay above government debt, so a low spread means lenders are barely pricing in the risk of not being repaid.

## The other set of numbers from the same week

@@CHK@@Labour force participation (July)|61.4%|Full-time employed (July)|133.55 million|High-yield spread (Aug 13)|2.71 points@@The first two are down 0.7 percentage points and 888,000 since January. The third moved the other way over the same stretch. What lenders fear and what workers face are heading in opposite directions.@@Retrieved 2026-08-16 · FRED (CIVPART · LNS12500000 · BAMLH0A0HYM2)

Participation measures the share of working-age Americans who either hold a job or are looking for one.
People who stop looking drop out of the unemployment count too, so the unemployment rate never shows them.
July saw 264,000 leave, June 720,000, and since last November the total exceeds 2.4 million.

Households are moving the same way.
Credit card delinquencies of 90 days or more stood at 12.9% in the second quarter, the second-highest reading since the first quarter of 2011.
The post-crisis peak was 13.7%, so this is not far from it.
Student loan delinquencies are at 10.6%, the highest since early 2020, and auto loans at 5.5%, the second-highest on record.

## Where the easy money went

@@SHARE@@Nvidia|10 points|10|Apple, Microsoft, Broadcom, Alphabet|about 15 points|15|The other 495 stocks|about 59 points|59@@Five names produced roughly 25 of the 84 percentage points the S&P 500 returned over five years, close to 30% of the total. Easy money did not lift the market evenly; it crowded into a narrow strip.@@The Kobeissi Letter post, 2026-08-15 · retrieved 2026-08-16

Other figures from the same week lean the same way.
The share of US consumers expecting higher share prices a year out reached 41.4% in July, the highest since April 2021, and speculative long dollar positioning hit 48 billion dollars, the largest since 2015 after quadrupling in three months.

Expectations and positions swelled on the asset side; delinquencies and participation gave way on the household side.
Same country, same week.

## JOLTS, measured by a 30% response rate

One more thing sits underneath all of this.
The surveys that produce those labour numbers are not being answered the way they once were.
Kobeissi reported on 15 August that only about one in four businesses now agree to take part in the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, and that roughly 30% file in time for the first estimate.

@@REF@@Federal Statistics: Stakeholders Said Jobs Report Generally Meets Their Needs, but Opportunities Exist to Improve Data Quality (US Government Accountability Office, GAO-26-107538, 2026-06-02)|https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-26-107538|https://www.gao.gov/assets/extracts/3634bdab0eb31cd0d8c37cb3b0d3f3a9/rId25_image6.png

The Government Accountability Office confirmed on 2 June that response rates fell for both the household and the establishment surveys from October 2015 through September 2025.
Its conclusion, though, is more careful than Kobeissi's.
For the household survey it recorded internal assessments finding limited effects on accuracy.
For the establishment survey it recorded that the Bureau of Labor Statistics has not yet released its assessment.
Participation comes from the household survey; job openings come from the establishment survey.
The side without a published assessment is the side markets stared at hardest this week.

So the contradiction runs two layers deep.
Easy money against strained households is one layer.
One of the two instruments measuring those households having no published verification is the second.
If participation slips further from here into the September FOMC and card delinquencies climb with it, easy financial conditions are running on a separate track from the real economy; if either one turns back, this exit reads as a single summer.
hanke-hormuz-9m-claim-vs-tracked-1_74m:
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the oil leaving the Strait of Hormuz is running at close to 9 million barrels a day on a seven-day average.
The firms that count the same strait with satellites and ship signals report numbers far below that.

@@REF@@Wright claims Persian Gulf oil trade is back at pre-Iran-war levels (Washington Examiner, 2026-08-12)|https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/energy-and-environment/4683048/chris-wright-claims-persian-gulf-oil-trade-pre-iran-war-levels/|https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-collage-cpi5u167u-1782322561169-e1782324080180.jpg?1786457655&resize=1200,683

The Strait of Hormuz is the only sea exit from the Persian Gulf.
How much oil moves through it sets the floor under the world oil price.

## What the strait carried before

@@BAR@@Normal traffic (first half of 2025)|20.9 million barrels a day|2090|Energy Secretary's seven-day average|9 million barrels a day|900|Kpler figure cited by Hanke (week of August 3)|1.74 million barrels a day|174@@All three numbers describe the same strait. Which one you pick changes the amount of oil the world is currently losing by more than tenfold.@@US Energy Information Administration, World Oil Transit Chokepoints (updated 2026-03-03) · Secretary Wright's post (2026-08-11) · Kpler figure cited by Hanke (2026-08-15) · retrieved 2026-08-16

The Energy Information Administration put flows through the strait at 20.9 million barrels a day in the first half of 2025.
That is one quarter of all crude oil traded by sea passing through a single narrow channel.

## The split is over what gets counted

@@CMP@@The Secretary's reading|Count everything leaving the Gulf. Add the 5 to 7 million barrels a day moving through new bypass pipelines to what crosses the strait and the total is not far from pre-war levels.|The ship-trackers' reading|Count only the vessels that actually transit. Oil in a pipeline never crossed the strait, and a ship with its position signal switched off cannot be counted at all.

Both sides are looking at the same water and drawing the boundary of the count in different places.

The interesting part is that the critics do not agree with each other either.
Commodity analyst Rory Johnston puts the seven-day average at about 7 million barrels a day and calls 9 million a stretch; Gregory Brew of Eurasia Group puts it near 5 million.
The Kpler figure Hanke cites is another three times smaller than that.

@@REF@@Tanker data challenges US claim of Gulf oil flow recovery (AGBI, 2026-08-12)|https://www.agbi.com/analysis/oil-and-gas/2026/08/tanker-data-challenges-us-claim-of-gulf-oil-flow-recovery/|https://www.agbi.com/tachyon/sites/4/2026/08/2026-07-14T120508Z_2066010026_MT1SIPA000CY121T_RTRMADP_3_SIPA-USA-scaled.jpg

Counting hulls instead of barrels sharpens the picture.
Kpler's ten-day average came to 11 transits a day, against more than 20 a day before the crisis.

## What the bypass pipelines can actually carry

The largest single line in the Secretary's arithmetic is the oil that skips the strait entirely.
Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline can nominally push 7 million barrels a day across the country.

The Red Sea terminal at Yanbu where that oil is loaded, however, can only handle 4.5 to 5 million barrels a day.
A wide pipe into a narrow port exports at the rate of the port.

The Emirati line to Fujairah currently runs 1.8 million barrels a day, and the work to roughly double it is about half finished, targeted at 2027.
That is why Johnston measures actual pipeline throughput at around 4 million barrels a day.

@@REF@@Gulf states race to build Hormuz bypass infrastructure (Kpler, 2026-07-10)|https://www.kpler.com/blog/new-pipelines-bypassing-the-strait-of-hormuz-could-come-online-in-1-2-years|https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65059ad784ac02253c62356c/6a58b9d872b4d22f22e4a70d_thumbnail_Strait_of_Hormuz_77077bdae8.jpg

## August 14, and two Emirati tankers

Hanke wrote that 56 tankers crossed the strait on August 14 last year and 4 crossed on the same date this year.
That single day's count cannot be verified from public data, but what happened that day can.

@@REF@@UAE accuses Iran of attacks on two state oil company vessels in the Strait of Hormuz (Al Jazeera, 2026-08-14)|https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/14/uae-accuses-iran-of-attacks-on-two-adnoc-vessels-in-strait-of-hormuz|https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/getty_6a7e5499b4-1786664089.jpg?resize=1920%2C1440

The United Arab Emirates said two tankers belonging to its state oil company were attacked in the strait that day.
The thin traffic is not a quirk of the statistics. It is attached to what happened on the water.

The price of passage tells the same story.
War risk premiums that ran at a quarter of one percent of hull value before the conflict now run between 3% and 10%.
For a $200 million tanker that is millions of dollars in premium for a single voyage, which means owners are staying away not because the channel is blocked but because the arithmetic no longer works.

So the argument is less about who is right than about which number you plan the next quarter around.
If Kpler's weekly average climbs above 9 million barrels a day before the end of the fourth quarter, the Secretary's account is supported; if it stays under that line through the quarter, the ship data was the better guide.

America's job-openings figure is built from the roughly one in four businesses that agree to answer, the source says.
Before the pandemic, the source says, that share ran between half and seven in ten.

@@REF@@Fewer people, businesses are responding to government requests for data (Marketplace, 2025-08-13)|https://www.marketplace.org/story/2025/08/13/what-happens-when-government-survey-participation-falls|https://img.apmcdn.org/4fccee7917ce412e8b1ffa7e2faca7ab401deb9b/widescreen/cd44ec-20250813-executive-woman-hand-filling-out-form-2000.jpg

Reporting on the same trend uses a slightly different yardstick.
The share of businesses taking part in government surveys fell from 75% in 2015 to 35% in April 2025.

@@BAR@@Business participation, 2015|75%|75|April 2025|35%|35@@That is how much of the answering side disappeared in ten years. The surveys did not get harder to fill in. The firms stopped filling them in.@@Marketplace, 2025-08-13, citing BLS figures. Retrieved 2026-08-16.

## A survey that waits 45 days for an answer

The Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey draws a sample of 21,000 establishments and collects answers over about 45 days.
Nobody is legally required to reply. Only the firms that want to reply do.

The release date arrives before the answers do.
So the BLS publishes a number from whatever has come in, then corrects it the following month as the late answers land.
The June openings figure came out on August 4, and on the same day May was cut by 57,000.

@@CHK@@June job openings|7.4 million|June unemployed|7.1 million|Openings per unemployed worker|1.0@@A labor market sitting at neither tight nor slack. The call turns on the first decimal place, and the sample that produces that decimal is thinning out.@@US Bureau of Labor Statistics, released 2026-08-04 for June, TED post 2026-08-07. Retrieved 2026-08-16.

One opening for every unemployed worker.
This is one of the ratios the Federal Reserve is known to reach for when it asks whether the labor market is running hot, and job openings are the numerator.
Shake the numerator and you shake the judgment.

## The budget behind the missing replies

The BLS budget was $636 million in fiscal 2025.
The fiscal 2026 request came in at $580 million, down 11.8%, and the same document carries a plan to cut staff by 17%.
When the money went, the collecting went first.
Consumer price collection stopped in Lincoln, Nebraska and Provo, Utah in April 2025, and in Buffalo, New York in May.
Three hundred and fifty detailed producer price indexes were dropped, and two federal advisory committees that watched over economic statistics were closed in March 2025.

@@REF@@A Long-Overdue Reckoning For The Bureau Of Labor Statistics (Forbes, 2025-08-13)|https://www.forbes.com/sites/georgecalhoun/2025/08/13/a-long-overdue-reckoning-for-the-bureau-of-labor-statistics/|https://imageio.forbes.com/specials-images/imageserve/689cc825723be15e7caa6bc4/0x0.jpg?format=jpg&height=900&width=1600&fit=bounds

That piece reads the problem not as a mistake by the agency but as a bill that had been deferred for years.
What went missing is not the numbers. It is the people and the legwork that make the numbers.

## June, recalculated on September 1

None of this is hidden.
Since March 13, 2026 the BLS has been publishing the response-rate series for the job openings survey in its public database.
Few people read it.

July job openings arrive on September 1, and June gets corrected the same day.
If the correction is smaller than 57,000, the late answers cannot move the first print much.
If it is bigger, then a market that has been reading each first print at face value has been trading a different number every month.
Either way, the thing worth watching is not how high job openings are. It is how far the figure travels afterwards.

## Why the date matters more than the price

In commodity markets the later delivery is usually the dearer one.
Storage and financing costs get added on top.

When that order flips and the immediate delivery becomes the expensive one, the market is in backwardation.
Put simply, there is not enough metal in the warehouse, so whoever cannot wait pays a premium to jump the queue.
The binding question stops being what copper costs and becomes when you can actually take hold of it.

A front position trading hundreds of dollars a tonne above the one behind it says a great many buyers cannot afford to be without metal right now.@@Figures as reported by Mining.com, 2026-08-14, accessed 2026-08-15

## The copper did not disappear, it moved

@@FLOW@@Tariff signalled|The market comes to expect a US duty on refined copper|Metal relocates|Producers and traders ship copper into US warehouses before any duty lands|London stocks drain|What is left in London shrinks while withdrawal requests pile up|Front premium|Buyers who need metal now pay far above those content to wait a month@@The copper was not consumed, it crossed the Atlantic. That is why this squeeze will not be undone by mines digging faster, and why it turns first on how the tariff is written.

There is one thing the Kobeissi Letter did not mention.

@@REF@@Indonesia smelter failure extends copper record rally as global stockpiles near crisis (TechTimes, 2026-08-11)|https://www.techtimes.com/articles/323984/20260811/indonesia-smelter-failure-extends-copper-record-rally-global-stockpiles-near-crisis.htm|https://d.techtimes.com/en/full/472271/indonesia-smelter-failure-extends-copper-record-rally-as-global-stockpiles-near-crisis.jpg

On August 8 a boiler water leak shut the Gresik smelter in East Java, Indonesia, for checks and repairs.
The plant makes about 342,000 tonnes of copper cathode a year and takes its ore solely from Grasberg, the second largest copper mine in the world.
It is owned jointly by Freeport Indonesia and Japan's Mitsubishi Materials.

If the pre-tariff shipments pulled existing copper to one side of the ocean, the outage cut the amount coming out of the ground into metal for several weeks.
The original post covers the first force. The second arrived at the same moment and pushed the same way.

## The numbers on the table are 15 percent in 2027 and 30 percent in 2028

What the market is really pricing is not copper supply and demand but a decision in Washington.
A phased duty is being discussed, with talk of 15 percent from 2027 rising to 30 percent from 2028.

If those numbers are confirmed, the copper already moved into the United States turns out to have been bought before the price of entry went up, and emptying the London sheds looks like a gain rather than a loss.
A lower or delayed duty flips it.
The metal parked in US warehouses gains a reason to come back out, and today's premium on immediate delivery goes away quickly.

So the thing to watch here is not the daily copper price but how fast the booked metal actually leaves the warehouses, and when the tariff decision lands.
Which of those two moves first will settle whether today's price was justified.
elerian-blanchard-france-multiple-equili:
The expectation that the European Central Bank will buy your government bonds comes with conditions that are written down.
The first one is not being subject to an excessive deficit procedure, or, if subject to one, not being assessed as having failed to take effective action in response to a Council recommendation.
France has been subject to that procedure since July 2024.

@@REF@@The Transmission Protection Instrument (European Central Bank press release, 2022-07-21)|https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2022/html/ecb.pr220721~973e6e7273.en.html|https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/shared/img/socialmedia/social-default.jpg?0ef1632c35edede913681bb76af694a4

The reason this comes up now is a post Olivier Blanchard wrote on August 15 about France's public finances, which Mohamed El-Erian passed along with the note that the framework fits some other economies too.

## What the phrase multiple equilibria points at

Multiple equilibria describes a situation in which the same conditions can produce two different outcomes.
If investors believe the debt is safe, rates stay low and it can indeed be serviced; if they believe it is unsafe, rates rise and servicing really does become hard.
Belief produces the outcome.

It works like a run on a bank.
If everyone thinks the money is there, it is; if everyone goes to withdraw at once, it genuinely is not.

@@FLOW@@Safe zone|Debt is clearly serviceable and the central bank has nothing to do|Danger zone|A good outcome and a bad one sit side by side, and the bad one is avoided if the central bank buys when private investors sell|Default zone|Debt is clearly not serviceable, fiscal policy has to be adjusted first, and this is not the central bank's job@@Each zone calls for a different response, so not knowing which one you are standing in means not being able to pick the response.

This is where Blanchard puts his finger.
When investors demand a higher risk premium, the central bank does not know for sure whether this is the danger zone, where it should step in, or already the default zone, where absent an adjustment programme it should not.
So it leans toward asking for the programme first, and counting on it to remove the bad equilibrium on its own, he wrote, is unwise.

## Which zone France is standing in

@@BAR@@France|117.6%|117.6|Italy|138.9%|138.9|Euro area average|88.9%|88.9|Germany|64.4%|64.4@@Countries sharing one currency sit this far apart. That is why no single number draws the line where the danger zone begins.@@Retrieved 2026-08-15 · Eurostat government debt release (2026-07-21) · Q1 2026

@@REF@@Government debt in the euro area, first quarter of 2026 (Eurostat, 2026-07-21)|https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-euro-indicators/w/2-21072026-ap|https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/2995521/18500178/New Africa_AdobeStock_521389990_RV.jpg/6d6a3c42-5eb3-03d6-555d-a19fafaa1117

The rating agencies have moved one way.
Moody's cut in December 2024, Fitch followed in September 2025 and S&P in October 2025.
France now carries A+ at S&P and Fitch, and one notch above that at Moody's, which is the only one attaching a negative outlook.
That is not the rating of a country facing default, and it is not a rating that tells you the country is in the safe zone either.
It is closest to the middle of Blanchard's three zones, and the middle is precisely the one where the answer is not settled.

## The four lines written on July 21, 2022

When the ECB created a purchase tool called the Transmission Protection Instrument on July 21, 2022, it published four eligibility criteria alongside it.
Compliance with the EU fiscal framework, the absence of severe macroeconomic imbalances, debt sustainability, and sound and sustainable macroeconomic policies.

The first criterion reads as not being subject to an excessive deficit procedure, or not being assessed as having failed to take effective action in response to an EU Council recommendation.
France entered that procedure on July 26, 2024, and on January 21, 2025 the Council adopted a recommendation to correct the deficit by 2029.
The European Commission's compliance report of June 3, 2026 still lists France among the countries with an open procedure.

The conjunction in that sentence carries weight.
Being subject to the procedure does not by itself remove eligibility; eligibility survives if the country is assessed as taking effective action.
France's standing therefore rests with the Commission's assessment rather than with the ECB.
Where Blanchard expects the central bank to ask for an adjustment programme first, he is restating something already set down as a condition.

No instance of the instrument actually being activated could be found.
That it has stood unused for four years is itself part of what has held markets in place.

How much of an expectation that the central bank will buy belongs in the price of the bonds is what splits here.
Fitch reviews France again on August 28.
If the rating holds, the ground stays where it is; one notch lower and the market starts reading the conditions instead.

Japan protested through diplomatic channels on July 31 after confirming that China had started installing another structure in the East China Sea.
The boundary between the two countries is still undelimited there, and by the count Japanese wires have kept, this is structure number twenty-four.

@@REF@@New movement by China concerning unilateral development of natural resources in the East China Sea (Japan MOFA, 2026-07-31)|https://www.mofa.go.jp/press/release/pressite_000001_02559.html

The ministry's own release does not say which number it is.

@@CHK@@Chinese structures confirmed by Japan (August 2025)|21|Same count (July 31, 2026)|24@@Three more in a year. The seabed is being occupied faster than the treaty clock runs.@@Retrieved 2026-08-15 · Japan MOFA release (2026-07-31) · Jiji Press and Nikkei counts

The water these structures stand in runs right up against the block Korea calls Block 7.

## What comes due on June 22, 2028

Block 7 sits on a sedimentary basin that begins south of Jeju Island.
It lies closer to Japan by distance, but the continental shelf under it runs back toward Korea, and in 1974 the two countries agreed to develop it together and split anything they found down the middle.
The agreement entered into force on June 22, 1978, for a term of fifty years.

@@REF@@Future of Korea-Japan joint development zone in doubt (Korea JoongAng Daily, 2024-02-14)|https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/korea/future-of-korea-japan-joint-development-zone-in-doubt/11509987|https://image.koreajoongangdaily.com/11510171.jpg?imageId=11510171&panox=0&panoy=0&panow=0&panoh=0&width=1200&height=683

Either side can end it with three years' notice, and the first day such notice could be given was June 22, 2025.
Japan did not give it that day, according to Yomiuri.

## Reading again the judgment that told Japan to wait

The original post locates Japan's patience in case law.
Natural prolongation, under which the country the shelf runs back to holds the rights, was the dominant doctrine into the 1970s, and the account has the International Court of Justice overturning that in the 1985 Libya-Malta case by ruling for a median line.

Open the judgment and the step does not land there.
The Court declined Malta's argument that equidistance had to be the mandatory starting point, and wrote that natural prolongation and distance are complementary rather than exclusive.
The drift is real: within 200 nautical miles, geological prolongation carries less legal weight than it once did.
What is not in that judgment is a sentence settling the question on a median line.
What kept Japan waiting is a probability leaning one way, not a decided rule.

There is a second place the original does not go.
China and Japan already agreed, in 2008, to develop this same stretch of sea jointly.

@@REF@@Delving deeper: China tests new waters in East China Sea oil and gas (CSIS Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative)|https://amti.csis.org/delving-deeper-china-tests-new-waters-in-east-china-sea-oil-and-gas/|https://amti.csis.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/North-ECS-jack-up-April-5-2026-banner.jpg

That agreement has gone eighteen years without being operationalised, and in the meantime China put its platforms up on the west side of the median line.
Signing something and then running out the clock has already produced one result in this water.

## The path by which Block 7 becomes disputed water

@@FLOW@@June 22, 2028|The Korea-Japan joint development agreement lapses after fifty years|Undelimited water|Neither side is left with settled ground to work it alone|One more party|China gains a place to argue, on natural prolongation, that it holds a share too@@What Japan may gain by waiting is not an exclusive licence but a sea with one more country in the arithmetic.

Korea cannot simply climb onto China's natural prolongation argument either.
China has a broad shelf, and conceding that logic unsettles the Yellow Sea, which the two countries divided on a median line.

The day for giving notice has passed, and less than two years are left.
If Japan moves toward splitting the shares with Korea again, this stays a problem between two countries.
If June 22, 2028 arrives with no notice given, the seabed gets settled before the law does.
The structures keep going up while that runs.

The person who put that number back into circulation is Steve Hanke, a monetary economist.
In the same post he named a single cause.
Cheap Russian gas was cut off, and Germany is at war with Russia, and this is turning the country into an industrial wasteland.

Naming a cause is the kind of claim you can check.
If the price of gas is the culprit, the industries that burn the most gas should be the ones falling apart.

## The industries that burn the most gas

In German manufacturing, the biggest gas consumer is chemicals and pharmaceuticals.
Gas heats their plants, and it is also the raw material that becomes plastics and fertiliser.
Car plants, by comparison, lean on electricity more than on gas.

The accounting firm EY counted German industrial employment for the whole of 2025.
The sector lost 124,000 jobs, and about 50,000 of them were in cars.
Chemicals and pharmaceuticals lost about 2,000.

The cause Hanke names does not explain that gap.@@Retrieved 2026-08-15 · EY analysis of German industrial employment (dpa, 2026-02-17) · German Federal Statistical Office, H1 2026 count (dpa, 2026-08-14)

The cheap Russian gas Germany used to import has been off since 2022.|Marina Burity · CC BY-SA 2.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gas_stove_blue_flames.jpg

In the same study EY listed its own reasons.
German carmakers are moving production abroad, and industrial revenue has fallen almost 5% since 2023.
Energy prices do not appear on that list as a standalone item.

## The segment that added people

Break the statistical office's count into segments and the direction is not uniform.
Parts and accessories makers were down 7.6%, and vehicle manufacturers were down 6.1%.
Bodywork and trailer makers, though, were up 10%, to 42,800.

All three pay the same gas price and the same electricity bill in the same country.
Explain everything with energy and the third segment is left over.

Put simply, this looks less like the whole plant losing power and more like specific lines losing orders.
Bodywork and trailers ride commercial and specialty vehicle demand, while parts suppliers take the full force of production moving abroad and of Chinese competitors.
When two groups pay the same fuel bill and one shrinks while the other grows, what separated them is the order book, not the meter.

## Between 42,300 and 47,000

Hanke's 42,400 differs from the statistical office count by 100. That looks like rounding.
The German automotive industry association published a different survey in February.
It put 2025 employment in the sector at 726,000 and said the year had cost 47,000 jobs.
The scope and the timing differ, so the numbers differ. Which one you quote moves the decline by nearly 5,000 people.

What is at stake is when to look at European auto suppliers again.
If energy costs are the cause, employment returns as gas prices come down.
If the cause is relocation and competition, the decline continues regardless of gas.
If the statistical office's next half-year count, due in August 2027, falls below this year's level again, the cause sits outside energy.
